readerTitle: Kraft Heinz cut costs to the bone. Then the bill came due.
caseNote: 실제 기업 (Kraft Heinz, 3G Capital, Berkshire Hathaway) + 가상 적용 (소프트웨어 회사)
insight: 제로 기반 예산은 낭비를 찾는 데 강하지만, 효과가 늦게 나타나는 투자를 같은 잣대로 심사하면 미래 매출을 깎는 도구가 된다.
misconception: 올해 효과를 증명하지 못하는 지출은 모두 낭비이고, 비용이 낮을수록 건강한 회사다.

sources.text: 3G Capital과 Berkshire Hathaway의 Heinz 인수(2013) 및 Kraft와의 합병(2015): 당시 양사 보도자료와 주요 언론 보도
Kraft Heinz, 2018년 4분기 실적 발표(2019년 2월 21일): 약 154억 달러 브랜드 가치 상각, 배당 삭감, SEC 조사 공개
Warren Buffett, CNBC 인터뷰(2019년 2월 25일): Kraft 인수가가 너무 높았다는 발언
Kraft Heinz CEO 교체(2019년, Miguel Patricio 취임) 관련 회사 발표
제로 기반 예산에 대한 일반적 설명: 관리회계 표준 개념

factChecks.note: Heinz 인수 2013년(3G Capital + Berkshire Hathaway), Kraft 합병 2015년 연도를 보도자료로 확인하세요.
2019년 2월 상각액 약 154억 달러(Kraft, Oscar Mayer 브랜드 등)를 실적 발표 원문으로 확인하세요. 카드에는 "about $15 billion"으로 적었습니다.
발표 다음 날 주가 하락폭(약 27%로 보도됨)과 배당 삭감폭(약 36%로 보도됨)을 확인하세요. 카드에는 "more than a quarter", "cut its dividend"로만 적었습니다.
SEC 조사는 구매(procurement) 관련 회계에 대한 것으로 보도되었습니다. 카드에는 세부 내용 없이 "an SEC investigation into its accounting"으로 적었습니다.
Buffett 발언은 직접 인용하지 않고 "said Berkshire had overpaid"로 요약했습니다. CNBC 인터뷰 원문으로 의미를 확인하세요.
제로 기반 예산이 브랜드·혁신 투자를 약화시켰다는 주장은 애널리스트와 언론의 해석이며 확정된 인과관계가 아닙니다. 카드에서도 "critics argued"와 다른 원인(인수가, 소비자 취향 변화)을 함께 적었습니다.
합병 당시 발표된 비용 절감 목표 수치(연 15억 달러로 보도됨)는 확인 전이라 카드에 넣지 않았습니다.

cards.title: Kraft Heinz cut costs to the bone. Then the bill came due.
body: After 2015, Kraft Heinz was praised for some of the fattest profit margins in packaged food. Its method: make every manager rebuild their budget from zero, every year.
In February 2019, the company wrote down the value of its famous brands by about **$15 billion**. What went wrong?

image.label: A pantry shelf of plain food jars with a shrinking budget ledger
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 식료품 선반 위 소스 병과 치즈 상자들(라벨은 무지, 실제 상표·로고 금지). 앞에 장부가 놓여 있고, 숫자 줄이 점점 짧아지며 마지막 줄은 0. 선반 일부 제품이 살짝 바래 보이게.

cards.title: Every dollar must be justified from zero.
body: It's 2015. You run a food brand inside the newly merged Kraft Heinz. The new owners say no line in last year's budget is safe. You must defend each cost as if starting fresh.
Your marketing and recipe-development spend builds the brand over years. You can't prove it pays back this year. What do you propose?

options.text: Cut it. If it can't show a return this year, it's waste
options.feedback: You'd look great on this year's margin. But brand strength fades slowly, so the cost shows up years later as lost sales.

options.text: Keep last year's amount plus inflation, since it has always worked
options.feedback: You protect the brand, but you skip the useful part of the exercise. Some of that spend may truly be wasted, and nobody checks.

options.text: Rebuild it from zero, but judge it on long-term signals like repeat buying, not this year's payback
options.feedback: You still hunt for waste, but you use a test that fits slow-payback spending. It's harder to defend in a cost-cutting culture.

cards.title: A famous cost machine.
body: Brazilian investment firm 3G Capital, with Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway, bought Heinz in 2013 and merged it with Kraft in 2015.
3G was known for one tool: **zero-based budgeting**. Managers closed plants, cut jobs, trimmed travel and marketing, and questioned every expense.
For a while it worked. Margins rose well above most rivals, and investors cheered.

cards.title: Zero-based budgeting
body: Most budgets are *incremental*: take last year's number and adjust it a little. That's quick, but old waste survives forever.
**Zero-based budgeting** starts every line at zero. Each cost must be explained and approved again, as if the business were brand new.
It's a powerful way to find spending nobody remembers approving. The catch is in what's easy to justify and what isn't.

image.label: Two budget columns: last year plus a bit vs starting from zero
image.brief: 두 개의 막대 비교 인포그래픽. 왼쪽 "Incremental: last year + 3%"는 이전 막대 위에 작은 블록이 얹힘. 오른쪽 "Zero-based"는 빈 바닥에서 블록을 하나씩 정당화하며 쌓음. 각 블록에 체크 표시.

cards.title: February 2019.
body: Kraft Heinz reported the roughly $15 billion write-down, mostly on its Kraft and Oscar Mayer brands. It also cut its dividend and disclosed an SEC investigation into its accounting.
The share price fell by **more than a quarter** in a day. Buffett said publicly that Berkshire had overpaid for Kraft.
Later that year, a new CEO took over and talked about investing more in the brands again.

cards.title: Cuts are easy to prove. Their costs are not.
body: A cut shows up in this year's numbers right away. A weaker brand shows up slowly: fewer new products, less advertising, shoppers drifting to fresher food and store brands.
Critics argued that Kraft Heinz trimmed exactly the spending that kept its brands growing, because that spending was the hardest to defend line by line.
Zero-based budgeting judged everything on proof. **Investments in the future rarely come with proof up front.**

image.label: A saw cutting a branch that supports a growing plant
image.brief: 일러스트. 가지치기 톱이 마른 잔가지("unused costs")를 자르다가 화분을 받치는 굵은 줄기("brand building")까지 자르려는 장면. 줄기 위에 아직 작은 새싹. 로고 없음.

cards.title: Don't blame the tool for everything.
body: Kraft Heinz had other problems. Many observers said the price paid for Kraft was too high, and tastes were already moving away from processed food. How much the budgeting itself hurt is still debated.

Many companies use zero-based budgeting well. It works best on running costs, like suppliers, travel and software subscriptions. It works worst when the same strict payback test is applied to slow investments.

cards.title: Now it's a software company.
body: Your software company runs its first zero-based review. Three items are on the table: unused tool subscriptions, a customer onboarding team, and a feature your engineers think will cut churn (customers leaving) next year.
How do you handle them?

options.text: Cut anything that can't show a return this quarter, including onboarding and the feature
options.feedback: Your costs drop fast. But if onboarding keeps users from leaving, churn rises later and erases the savings.

options.text: Cancel unused subscriptions; keep onboarding and the feature, tied to churn targets you review each quarter
options.feedback: Running costs get the strict test; investments get a fair one with clear early signals. You still need the discipline to stop them if the signals stay flat.

options.text: Skip the review and trim every line by 10%
options.feedback: Simple and quick, but it cuts good and wasteful spending alike, and the unused subscriptions mostly survive.

cards.title: Start from zero, but don't judge seeds like weeds.
body: Zero-based budgeting finds waste. Used only to cut, it also removes the spending that makes future sales.
**Try it today:** split your budget into two lists: costs of running the business and investments in its future. Give each list its own test.
